items.title: Adding Liquidity to Meteora: A Pool Creation Guide
items.tldr: Step by step through DAMM v2 pool creation and fee configuration, which is the part where a small misconfiguration quietly costs you for the life of the pool.

items.title: How to Create a Liquidity Pool for Your Solana Token
items.tldr: Compares Raydium and Meteora pool types and walks the setup. Genuinely useful because pool choice is made once and is awkward to undo afterwards.

items.title: How to Create and Deploy Your Own ERC-20 Token
items.tldr: A deployment walkthrough on a new EVM chain. Worth reading for what the standard actually requires versus what tooling adds on top.

items.title: Driving Saturn's Revolution in Bitcoin DeFi
items.tldr: An engineering account of building DeFi where the base layer offers almost no programmability. The constraints are the interesting part.

items.title: Engineering tBTC on Sui: Bitcoin's First Live Non-EVM Integration
items.tldr: Porting a Bitcoin bridge to a chain with a completely different object model. Interesting for the assumptions that turned out to be EVM-specific rather than universal.

items.title: Broad Onchain Contraction Defined Crypto Markets in H1 2026
items.tldr: A short data note arguing the contraction was broad rather than concentrated in one sector. Useful as a counterweight to narratives built on a single chart.

items.title: Canonical Bridges vs Third-Party Bridges: What's the Difference?
items.tldr: One is the chain's own official route with its withdrawal delay; the other fronts liquidity to make it fast. They solve different jobs, and this is clear about when each is right.

items.title: Crosschain Swaps Explained: Swap and Bridge in One Transaction
items.tldr: Trading a token on one chain for a different token on another, without doing it as two steps. Walks through how the swap and the bridge get composed into a single action.

items.title: No Gas on a New Chain? How to Arrive With ETH Ready to Spend
items.tldr: Landing on a chain with assets you cannot move because you have no native token is a genuinely common trap. Explains how to arrive already able to transact.

items.title: Efficient Sorter: The Winning Solutions
items.tldr: Published solutions from a gas-optimisation contest. Reading how other people solved the same constrained problem is one of the fastest ways to improve at Solidity.

items.title: Fibonacci Neighbor: The Winning Solutions
items.tldr: Another set of contest answers, this time on an algorithmic challenge. Useful for seeing where clever maths beats clever code and where it does not.

items.title: Meet AgorApp
items.tldr: An interactive IDE for learning Web3 engineering by writing code rather than reading about it. Sets out the case for practice-first learning in a field that mostly ships documentation.

items.title: 5 New AI Apps Built on Akash
items.tldr: From simplified agent deployment to gesture-controlled glasses. Useful as evidence of what people actually build on decentralised compute rather than what it is pitched for.

items.title: AI's Infrastructure Problem Is Bigger Than the Grid
items.tldr: Close to half of US data centres planned for 2026 are expected to slip or be cancelled. Digs into causes that go well beyond power availability.

items.title: EVM Mirror: Mind the Gap Between Audit and Deployment
items.tldr: The code that was audited and the bytecode that ended up onchain are not always the same thing. On closing that gap, which is a quietly common source of risk.

items.title: Verifiable Secret Ballots With Interfold and Aragon
items.tldr: Onchain voting is transparent by default, which is exactly wrong for a secret ballot. Describes a CRISP-based implementation that keeps votes private while still verifiable.

items.title: Binance Arbitrage: Fee Optimization, API Limits and Strategies
items.tldr: The longest of the set, and the most practical: fee tiers, API rate limits, and triangular routes. Rate limits are what actually kill these strategies at scale.

items.title: Money Flow Index: A Complete Guide for Crypto Trading
items.tldr: A volume-weighted momentum indicator, explained properly rather than as a signal to copy. Covers divergence and where the reading misleads.

items.title: Binance-Bybit BTC Arbitrage: Strategy, Fees and Execution
items.tldr: Works a single pair between two venues in detail: identifying 0.3-0.5% spreads, then showing how taker fees decide whether the trade was ever profitable.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Coins vs Tokens: What's the Difference?
items.tldr: A coin has its own chain, a token borrows someone else's. The distinction sounds pedantic until it determines who can freeze your balance.

items.title: Blockchain and Parametric Insurance
items.tldr: Parametric policies pay out on a measured trigger rather than an assessed claim, which is exactly the shape a smart contract handles well. A good fit worth understanding.

items.title: Blockchain and the EU Digital Battery Passport
items.tldr: A regulated traceability requirement with real deadlines, which makes it one of the few enterprise blockchain cases driven by law rather than by interest.

items.title: Securing Solidity Smart Contracts: Essential Audit Insights
items.tldr: The longest piece here, covering common vulnerability classes, how to fix them, and where AI-driven tooling genuinely helps versus where it produces noise.

items.title: 3 Different Ways of Filing Your Crypto Taxes
items.tldr: Lays out the realistic options, from doing it yourself through software to handing everything to an accountant, with what each actually demands of your records.

items.title: Atomic Wallet Security
items.tldr: How the wallet handles keys, backups and recovery. Worth reading critically given the platform's own history, and useful as a checklist of what to ask any wallet.

items.title: Liquidity Pools: What They Are and How They Work
items.tldr: Starts from the pool itself, then automated market makers, the pool types that exist and what providing liquidity commits you to. Thorough for a beginner piece.

items.title: Blockaid's Response to the CFTC on Prediction Markets
items.tldr: A submitted comment letter on the CFTC's proposed public interest framework. Reading a real regulatory filing teaches more about the constraints than any summary of one.

items.title: Onchain Monitoring for Trading Firms: Real-Time Risk Visibility
items.tldr: A desk needs to know not just what it holds but everything those positions quietly depend on. On making that second layer visible while capital is still deployed.

items.title: Prop Desk to Curator: JPEG Trading's Security Evolution
items.tldr: A fast-moving book across 100+ protocols and 15+ chains, and what had to change operationally to keep it safe. Concrete case study rather than a capability list.

items.title: Adding a ZetaChain-EVM RPC Endpoint to MetaMask
items.tldr: A short walkthrough for pointing a wallet at a specific RPC provider. Doing this once makes clear how much your wallet depends on whoever answers those calls.

items.title: Building an AI Agent From Scratch
items.tldr: A minimal assistant written in TypeScript, used to strip agents down to their actual moving parts. Far more instructive than reading about frameworks.

items.title: Evaluating Agent Skills: Testing Whether They Are Actually Useful
items.tldr: 92 A/B evaluations run to measure whether agent skills genuinely improved capability. Rare in publishing a measurement rather than an impression.

items.title: RAG From the Ground Up
items.tldr: Builds retrieval-augmented generation from nothing: ingestion, retrieval, generation, and crucially how they evaluated whether it worked. The evaluation half is what most write-ups skip.

items.title: What Is Bundling in Crypto?
items.tldr: Grouping several transactions into one atomic execution so they either all land in order or none do. Explains why ordering guarantees matter far more than the gas saving.

items.title: Send Money Home Cheaper and Faster With Stablecoins
items.tldr: Traditional remittance takes an average 6.49% per transfer and several days. Compares that against a stablecoin route without pretending the last mile is solved.

items.title: What Is a Real-World Asset (RWA)? A Guide to RWAs on Base
items.tldr: Begins at the plainest definition, a Treasury bond or a bar of gold sitting off the chain, then builds up to how those get represented on Base and where you keep them safely.

items.title: Who Is Satoshi Nakamoto? The Suspects and the Hunt to Unmask Bitcoin's Creator
items.tldr: Seventeen years after the genesis block nobody has proved who Satoshi is. Goes through each named suspect and what the evidence really amounts to, which is usually less than reported.

items.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Ceramic's Private Data Proof-of-Concept
items.tldr: Adding privacy to a network built around open, shared data is genuinely awkward. Walks through a deliberately minimal proof of concept rather than promising a finished feature.

items.title: How Pairwise Synchronization Improves Decentralized Data Management
items.tldr: The team replaced the algorithm at the heart of the database, moving from multicast to pairwise sync. Explains what was wrong with the old approach and what the swap cost them.

items.title: OrbisDB Is a Practical Upgrade for Databases on Ceramic
items.tldr: What changes when you put a familiar database interface over a decentralised data network, and which of the usual guarantees survive that translation.

items.title: How to Run a Token Sale on Your Own Website
items.tldr: Hosting the sale yourself means owning the compliance, the contract and the failure modes that a launchpad would otherwise absorb. Practical about all three.

items.title: How to Ship a Token Launch That Runs as One Stack
items.tldr: Launches usually get assembled from four vendors that do not talk to each other. Argues for treating sale, vesting, staking and distribution as one system.

items.title: How to Ship Token Staking at TGE
items.tldr: Staking live on day one changes the circulating supply maths immediately. Covers what has to be ready before generation rather than bolted on weeks later.

items.title: From "Sandboxed" Evals to Production Exploits
items.tldr: A test environment that quietly reaches real infrastructure stops being a test. Uses a Hugging Face case to show how the line between evaluation and exploitation gets crossed.

items.title: The Rise of Spot Markets for Inference
items.tldr: Long first part on where inference marketplaces actually stand, the structural inefficiencies holding them back, and the pressures that may force them to change.

items.title: When Cyber Agents Go Off-Script
items.tldr: Giving an agent internet access and relying on the prompt to contain it is not a security boundary. Argues that combination reliably produces misconduct rather than occasionally.

items.title: "Insufficient Funds" in Your Wallet? Here's What's Actually Wrong
items.tldr: The error almost never means what it says. Six causes, nearly all of them about gas rather than balance, explained clearly enough to fix rather than guess at.

items.title: How to Choose a Wallet-as-a-Service Provider
items.tldr: A seven-step checklist covering key control, MPC security, approval flows and compliance. The key control question is the one that determines everything else.

items.title: Wallet-as-a-Service: What the Comparisons Skip
items.tldr: Most vendor comparisons weigh speed and cost. Argues the custody model is the variable that actually matters and the one nobody puts in the table.

items.title: Ten Projects Built on The Graph at ETHGlobal Lisbon
items.tldr: The interesting result is not who won but how many independent teams reached for the same data primitives. A read on what indexing gets used for in practice.

items.title: The Graph Technical Roadmap
items.tldr: Sets out multi-service blockchain data infrastructure on Horizon, a protocol intended to serve more than subgraph queries. Useful for seeing where indexing is heading.

items.title: Making Family Simpler and Safer
items.tldr: The follow-up covering what actually changed in onboarding. Worth reading alongside the first piece to see the argument turned into product decisions.

items.title: The Crypto Wallet Problem: Why We Created Family Accounts
items.tldr: Seed phrases put irreversible loss one mistake away, which no other consumer product does. A well-argued piece on why that model was never going to reach ordinary users.

items.title: Agent Wallets Compared: Crossmint, Privy, Turnkey, Coinbase
items.tldr: Long side-by-side of the main agent wallet providers. Vendor-authored, but detailed enough on key custody and spending limits to serve as a map of what this category has to solve.

items.title: Agentic Commerce Use Cases: 5 Examples That Work Today
items.tldr: Short and deliberately unambitious: five things agents can actually transact for right now, which is a useful corrective to the broader speculation.

items.title: What Is Account Abstraction? ERC-4337 Wallets Explained
items.tldr: A clean walk through what ERC-4337 changes about who pays gas, who signs, and what a wallet is allowed to be. Good grounding before anything agent-related makes sense.

items.title: Argentina's LIBRA Wallet Freeze: AML Screening at Scale
items.tldr: A judicial order naming 25 wallets, and what exchanges had to do about it across their books. Concrete illustration of why screening has to be programmatic rather than manual.

items.title: Uniswap v4 Permissioned Pools: On-Chain AML for Regulated DeFi
items.tldr: Compliance moving into the protocol layer changes who is responsible for screening and when it happens. Covers what that means for address checks and transaction monitoring.

items.title: x402 Payments: The Stablecoin Rail for AI Agents and APIs
items.tldr: HTTP 402 was reserved for payment and never used. Explains how a stablecoin paywall on an API endpoint finally gives it a purpose, and what an agent needs to satisfy it.

items.title: DAO Formation: A Legal Wrapper Guide
items.tldr: How to pick a wrapper and then keep it aligned with the governance and treasury controls you actually run. The ongoing maintenance section is the part most guides omit.

items.title: DAOs and AI Agents: A New Frontier or a Risk to Decentralization?
items.tldr: Automating governance removes the human bottleneck and also removes the human check. Balanced on the legal implications, which are further from settled than the technical ones.

items.title: Incentives and Coordination in DAOs: Build an Operating System, Not a Voting Machine
items.tldr: Argues DAOs rarely fail at voting and routinely fail at coordination. Mandates and incentive design get more attention here than governance mechanics, which is the right emphasis.

items.title: The Defx Liquidity Engine
items.tldr: What sits behind a perps DEX and how liquidity gets sourced and priced. Short, but one of the few places this layer is described rather than assumed.

items.title: Multi-Chain Apps and the Importance of Stateless Clients
items.tldr: Every extra chain an app touches adds another RPC endpoint you have to trust. Explains how stateless clients verify data locally with proofs instead of taking a provider's word.

items.title: Pragmatic Adaptive Privacy
items.tldr: Opens by admitting privacy was never a design goal of Bitcoin or Ethereum, which is why retrofitting it is so awkward. Long and unusually honest about the tradeoffs involved.

items.title: The Code Was Fine. That's the Problem.
items.tldr: A long post-mortem on the KelpDAO exploit arguing the failure was in the trust layer, not the contracts. Makes the case that cross-chain bridges need cryptographic verification rather than multisig assurance.

items.title: Best Solana Wallets
items.tldr: A survey aimed at people arriving at Solana for the first time, weighing custody model and recovery rather than which one looks nicest.

items.title: Centralised Exchange vs Decentralised Exchange
items.tldr: Sets the two models against each other on custody, listing control and what happens when something goes wrong, rather than treating it as an ideological question.

items.title: Price Action 101: Breakers
items.tldr: Part of a trading fundamentals series. Short, focused on one pattern, and explains what the structure is supposed to signal rather than just how to draw it.

items.title: 2026 Election Forecast Methodology Explained
items.tldr: Most forecast pages hand you a number and hide the recipe. This publishes the polling adjustments, how poll and market data get weighted against each other, and the scenario modelling.

items.title: Bitcoin Analysis: Reading the Market When It Crashes
items.tldr: A framework for reading a falling market rather than a prediction about one. Runs through the indicators and onchain signals that stay meaningful when price is moving fast.

items.title: DuelDuck for Beginners: A P2P Prediction Market Guide
items.tldr: In a peer-to-peer duel your counterparty is another user, not a house. Covers how a ticket gets priced, how Yes and No resolve, and when the USDC actually reaches you.

items.title: A Deep Dive Into TSS-MPC
items.tldr: What threshold signature schemes are, how they differ from other flavours of multi-party computation, and the security properties that follow from each choice.

items.title: Beyond the Speed Myth: TSS-MPC Performance
items.tldr: The standing objection to threshold signatures has been latency. Argues that objection is now several years out of date, and shows where the time actually goes.

items.title: Building Identity-Based Mini Apps With World ID
items.tldr: Gating an app on proof of personhood rather than on a wallet balance. A practical walkthrough of what verified human access changes about the design.

items.title: The Next Billion Wallets Won't Know They're Using Crypto
items.tldr: Argues the next wave of wallet users never self-identify as crypto users at all, and that stablecoins plus embedded wallets are what make that possible.

items.title: Why AI Agents Need Communication Infrastructure
items.tldr: An autonomous agent still has to receive information it can trust, on time. Short piece on what that channel has to guarantee before the agent can act on anything.

items.title: Euler Primer: The Credit Layer for Programmable Finance
items.tldr: The long-form case for treating lending as modular infrastructure rather than one monolithic pool, and what that unlocks that a shared-pool design cannot.

items.title: What Is the Ethereum Vault Connector?
items.tldr: Account infrastructure built around ERC-4626 that lets vaults be used as collateral for one another. The piece of plumbing that makes modular lending composable rather than isolated.

items.title: What Is the Euler Vault Kit?
items.tldr: The framework every Euler lending vault is built from. Start here if you want to understand what is actually configurable in a lending market and what is fixed.

items.title: Lost Keys, No Lost Land
items.tldr: The obvious objection to tokenised property is what happens when someone loses their keys. Nearly six thousand words answering exactly that, which is the right length for the question.

items.title: Tether for Land
items.tldr: Takes the comparison seriously rather than as a slogan: what it would mean for land titles to move the way a stablecoin does, and which parts of property law refuse to cooperate.

items.title: Title Insurance After Tokenization
items.tldr: Short, and the most concrete evidence in the set: a tokenised property went through a conventional sale and a major underwriter wrote the title policy. Theory meeting practice.

items.title: AWS S3 Pricing: What You'll Actually Pay
items.tldr: Storage is the cheap part. Requests, retrievals and egress are where the bill comes from, and this walks each line so the total stops being a surprise.

items.title: How Browser Uploads Work With Pre-Signed S3 URLs
items.tldr: Letting a browser upload straight to storage without handing it your credentials. Covers the backend signing step and the CORS configuration that trips everyone up.

items.title: Infura IPFS Is Shutting Down: How to Migrate
items.tldr: A concrete deadline and a concrete migration path for anyone with pins on Infura. Also a useful reminder that pinned does not mean permanent.

items.title: An End-to-End Encrypted Alternative to Google Docs
items.tldr: What actually changes when collaborative editing is encrypted by default, including the features that become harder to offer once the server cannot read the document.

items.title: Google Docs and Gemini AI: The Privacy Problem
items.tldr: Your documents are not end-to-end encrypted, which means the privacy question is entirely one of trust rather than of cryptography. Direct about what that implies.

items.title: Google Docs vs Microsoft Word: Which Is Better?
items.tldr: Compares the two on collaboration, formatting and offline editing, but the privacy and security section is the part worth your time.

items.title: Dev Workshop: Building an Onramp to Any Chain
items.tldr: Seven lines of code to a working onramp. Short, and a good measure of how far the integration burden for fiat-to-crypto has actually fallen.

items.title: Halliday: The First Workflow Protocol
items.tldr: As chains and services multiplied, the hard part stopped being any single call and became sequencing them reliably. Sets out workflows as the missing abstraction.

items.title: Deploying Smart Contracts Using Hardhat Ignition
items.tldr: Declarative deployment: describe the end state and let the tool work out the ordering and resume from failures. A better model than a script that must run perfectly once.

items.title: Displaying Execution Traces
items.tldr: Short, and disproportionately useful: seeing exactly which calls ran and what they returned is the fastest way to understand why a transaction reverted.

items.title: Managing Config Values and Secrets Safely
items.tldr: Private keys in a committed config file remain one of the most common ways teams lose funds. Covers the mechanism Hardhat provides so they never sit in the repo.

items.title: Breaking Down the sBTC-Wormhole Integration
items.tldr: Moving a Bitcoin-backed asset across chains means two different trust models meeting in the middle. Explains where the handoff happens and what each side assumes.

items.title: Deep Dive: How the Token Metadata API Works
items.tldr: Token metadata sounds trivial until you have to serve it consistently across standards and chains. A look at what the API actually has to reconcile.

items.title: Dissecting a Transaction Signature on Stacks
items.tldr: Pulls a signature apart field by field. Signature formats are usually treated as a black box, and understanding one properly makes a whole class of bugs legible.

items.title: LangChain and CrewAI Integration
items.tldr: Wiring live prices, DeFi analytics and token security checks into agent frameworks. Useful for seeing where an agent's data actually comes from.

items.title: MCP Integration Tutorial
items.tldr: Step by step for connecting Claude, Cursor or another MCP client to live crypto data. Practical, and a decent introduction to what MCP actually does.

items.title: REST API Tutorial
items.tldr: The plainest of the three: querying prices, yields and token security over HTTP, with no framework in the way. Start here if the others feel like too many layers.

items.title: Builder Journeys: Deploying Bridged USDC With Warp Routes
items.tldr: A team's actual path to getting bridged USDC live on their chain. Implementation detail of the kind that rarely makes it into documentation.

items.title: Builder Journeys: DIA Crosschain Oracle
items.tldr: How an oracle team delivered price data across chains, and which interoperability decisions they had to make first. Implementation detail rather than architecture diagram.

items.title: Builder Journeys: LogX Expands Trading Interchain
items.tldr: A trading venue extending across chains, told from the builder's side. Worth reading for what breaks when order flow and settlement stop sharing a chain.

items.title: Building With Modular Security Legos
items.tldr: Interoperability security is usually presented as one setting. This breaks it into composable modules you choose between, which makes the tradeoffs visible instead of implicit.

items.title: How Permissionless Is Your Interoperability Provider? A Checklist
items.tldr: A pointed set of questions to ask before depending on a bridge: who can add a chain, who can pause it, and who you need permission from. Uncomfortable for most providers.

items.title: 4 Security Testing Tools Every DeFi Developer Should Use Before Auditing
items.tldr: What to run yourself before paying anyone to audit, on the reasonable basis that auditors should not be spending their time on what a fuzzer would have caught.

items.title: 4 Wallet Security Myths That Put Users at Risk
items.tldr: Takes apart the reassuring beliefs people hold about hardware wallets and seed phrases, and is specific about what each myth actually leaves exposed.

items.title: A Mathematical Theory of Danksharding
items.tldr: Short and unapologetically formal. If you have read the accessible explanations of data availability sampling and want the actual mathematics, this is the step up.

items.title: AMD XDNA: Meet the ZK Acceleration King
items.tldr: Proof generation is now a hardware problem as much as a cryptographic one. Benchmarks a specific accelerator architecture against the workload ZK actually creates.

items.title: Bridging the Multichain Universe With Zero Knowledge Proofs
items.tldr: Long treatment of proof-based bridging, where the receiving chain verifies mathematics rather than trusting a validator set. The most rigorous answer to the bridge problem.

items.title: DAO Taxes: The Ultimate Guide
items.tldr: Governance tokens create tax positions that nobody agreed to take on. Covers how a DAO can stay compliant when the entity itself may not legally exist anywhere.

items.title: How to Prepare for the Transition to Account-Level Cost Basis
items.tldr: New IRS rules mandate wallet-by-wallet lot tracking rather than one pooled basis. If you have been reporting the old way, this is the change that forces a rebuild.

items.title: A Step-by-Step KYC Guide
items.tldr: Verification is where most people abandon a regulated platform. Useful mostly for showing exactly what gets asked for and why each item is required.

items.title: An Extensive Guide to Buying Your First Security Token
items.tldr: Security tokens carry transfer restrictions and eligibility checks that ordinary tokens do not. Walks a first purchase including the parts that will block you.

items.title: Deobfuscation Ratings, Inlining Fat Functions, and Breaking Opaque Predicates
items.tldr: Concrete techniques for undoing deliberate obfuscation. Directly relevant to anyone trying to understand what an unverified contract or binary actually does.

items.title: Mutation-Resistant Library Code Matching
items.tldr: Identifying known library code even after it has been altered to avoid detection. The cat-and-mouse framing makes the problem unusually easy to follow.

items.title: Reversing Nvidia GPU SASS Code
items.tldr: Long and deeply technical work on decompiling GPU assembly, a target with almost no tooling. Far outside the usual crypto reading and better for it.

items.title: Address Poisoning Attacks: How They Scam Web3 Users
items.tldr: The attack works because people verify the first and last few characters of an address and nothing in between. Covers detection and the habits that defeat it.

items.title: Human Behavior Causes 44% of Web3 Losses
items.tldr: Research putting nearly half of crypto theft down to human error rather than broken code, despite the billions spent on securing the code.

items.title: Solana Security: Automated Defense for Wallets and Programs
items.tldr: $250M lost on Solana in a single half-year, most of it to phishing and social engineering rather than protocol bugs. On catching those at transaction time.

items.title: A New Automation Fee Model
items.tldr: Moving away from charging per automation run. Worth reading for how fee design shapes whether users leave automation switched on at all.

items.title: How to Use Zap In on the Krystal Wallet App
items.tldr: Entering a liquidity position from a single token instead of assembling both sides yourself. Explains the swap happening underneath and what it costs you.

items.title: Flip Orders: Concentrated Liquidity on Order Books
items.tldr: Borrows the concentrated liquidity idea from AMMs and applies it to a CLOB, aiming for AMM-style simplicity without giving up order book control.

items.title: Introducing Vaults
items.tldr: Providing liquidity to an order book without managing individual orders yourself. Short, and useful for seeing what gets abstracted away and what you still carry.

items.title: What Does a Market Maker Do?
items.tldr: The clearest of the three: what market making actually involves, and how the job differs on an AMM versus a central limit order book. Good grounding before the others.

items.title: Agentic Finance: How AI Agents Work With Lagoon Vaults
items.tldr: Moving agents from chat to actual capital means letting them discover a vault, read its state, and act on it. Describes what each of those three steps requires.

items.title: Lagoon's Fee Structure: The Four Fee Types, Explained
items.tldr: Management, performance, entry/exit and protocol fees, with the actual formulas, caps and accrual mechanics rather than a summary. Rare to see a vault show this much of its arithmetic.

items.title: More Than Vaults: Lagoon's Open Data Layer
items.tldr: An SDK reading contracts directly, plus a public GraphQL API with no key required. Worth reading for the argument that vault data should be queryable by anyone, not just the operator.

items.title: A New Era for ZK: Decentralizing the ZK Stack
items.tldr: Proof generation concentrated in a few hands recreates the trust problem proofs were meant to remove. The longest piece here, and the clearest on why prover decentralisation matters.

items.title: AI Is Scaling Faster Than We Can Verify It
items.tldr: Model capability is outrunning any ability to check what a model actually did. Frames verifiable computation as the missing half rather than an optional extra.

items.title: Cheap and Fast Cross-Chain Queries With a ZK Coprocessor
items.tldr: Reading another chain's historical state normally means trusting whoever tells you about it. A concrete look at proving the answer instead of trusting it.

items.title: Making Gas Tokens a Thing of the Past
items.tldr: Opens on the familiar dead end of holding tokens you cannot move because you have no ETH for gas, then covers how paying fees in any asset removes it.

items.title: Most Tokens Will Never Reach Their ATH Again. Why?
items.tldr: Dilution is the answer, and it is a much less comfortable one than market sentiment. A short piece that reframes how to read a token's price history.

items.title: Trading With Onchain Data Instead of Guesswork
items.tldr: Nobody has a crystal ball, but most people trade with far less onchain information than is freely available. A survey of what data is worth watching.

items.title: Introducing Meld Network: Access Digital Assets Anywhere
items.tldr: The project's own statement of what it is building and why a dedicated network was the chosen route. Short, and the clearest single description available.

items.title: Introducing Midas Staked Liquidity: Atomic Liquidity for Tokenised Assets
items.tldr: Tokenised assets are easy to issue and awkward to exit. Describes a dedicated liquidity layer built specifically to make redemption instant rather than negotiated.

items.title: What Are Onchain Investment Products?
items.tldr: Traces the shift from lending pools and liquidity farming toward something structured like an actual financial product, and what has to exist for that to hold.

items.title: The Execution Gap in Onchain Asset Management
items.tldr: Having a strategy is the easy half. Getting it executed reliably, repeatedly, without someone watching a dashboard is where onchain asset management actually breaks down.

items.title: The Infrastructure Behind One-Click DeFi
items.tldr: One button on the surface, several of the hardest coordination problems in crypto underneath. Unpacks everything that has to line up between the click and settlement.

items.title: What Is Mimic?
items.tldr: The short version straight from the source: you define the logic, Mimic runs it, and you never deploy or babysit a contract yourself. Read this before the deeper pieces.

items.title: Introducing the Personal Crypto IBAN
items.tldr: A bank transfer arriving directly as crypto in your own wallet, and the reverse. The clearest example of the fiat boundary genuinely disappearing rather than being wrapped.

items.title: Zero Fees on the ZCHF Swiss Franc Stablecoin
items.tldr: Worth reading less for the fee change than for the introduction to Frankencoin itself, a Swiss franc stablecoin with a governance model unlike the dollar-backed majority.

items.title: AgentArena Case Study: Adversarial AI Security Analysis for Lido
items.tldr: Pointing adversarial agents at a live staking protocol to see what they find. Interesting for the methodology as much as the findings.

items.title: AuditAgent on EVMBench: What the Data Shows
